//: OpenRouter free-tier configuration. Tiers follow docs/LESSONS.md: the strongest model does the actual translation, reliable tool-callers do everything else. All are :free models with function calling (mandatory — every agent drives file tools) that keep reasoning in a separate field (no leak into output, satisfying LESSONS.md #4). smolagents reaches OpenRouter through LiteLLM: model ids are prefixed with 'openrouter/' and the key is read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Get a key at https://openrouter.ai/keys.
//model-choice: All tiers use nemotron-3-super here because smolagents always sends tool_choice='required', and this NVIDIA-hosted model answers that reliably where Venice-hosted models (qwen/llama) frequently return HTTP 429 'rate-limited upstream'. gpt-oss is avoided on purpose: besides 429s, live runs showed it leaking its raw harmony/channel control tokens into the text stream ('to=functions.read_file', stray role tokens) instead of emitting structured tool_calls, so its file writes silently never executed. The harness owns a single Retry-After backoff layer (src/lexis_smol/diagnostics.py sets retry=False on the base model to avoid double-retry stalls); each subagent's result also carries a harness-computed 'Files written this run:' line so the orchestrator never has to trust a model's self-report. If nemotron saturates too, check https://openrouter.ai/models for what's live and swap freely.
//limits: OpenRouter free (:free) models are shared upstream capacity: expect frequent HTTP 429 ('temporarily rate-limited upstream'), which the harness auto-retries with backoff. On top of that there is an ACCOUNT-WIDE daily cap across all free models: 50 requests/day by default, 1000/day after buying ~$10 of credits, plus ~20 req/min. A full ~100k-word novel runs on the order of ~1000 requests, so: 50 RPD = a chapter/day, a whole book over a couple of weeks (fine if unhurried — the git-checkpointed workspace resumes across days); 1000 RPD = a book in a day or two but you'll still wait through upstream-429 backoff. For a smooth run, add a little OpenRouter credit or your own upstream key (BYOK), or use the commented Anthropic paid block (no daily cap, a few dollars per book).

agent_overrides.//: Per-agent experiments — keys here override the agent's tier spec. For higher translation quality when available, try openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free (550B, 1M ctx). Qwen is the multilingual king (openrouter/qwen/qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct:free) but is usually Venice-hosted and 429-saturated.

pricing.//: $/MTok fallback for cost display. The :free models above cost $0; LiteLLM reports $0 (or unknown → $0) for them, so no entries are needed here. These entries apply if you swap in paid models.
